_about: Curated starting list of well-known US high school programs. Deadlines, costs and eligibility change every cycle: treat every field as a lead and confirm it on the official page before acting (/search does this automatically). deadline_month is the usual month the main deadline falls in (1-12), used only for sorting and early warnings.

programs.name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
programs.org: Center for Excellence in Education / MIT
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors; separate international nomination routes
programs.notes: 6-week research internship; strong test scores and prior research help

programs.name: MIT PRIMES
programs.eligibility_notes: Main program for Boston-area students; PRIMES-USA for others (math)
programs.notes: Application includes a problem set

programs.name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
programs.eligibility_notes: Open only to juniors at time of applying; need-blind, meets full need
programs.notes: Team research project in 5-6 weeks

programs.name: Simons Summer Research Program
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors; US citizens or permanent residents
programs.notes: Students join a faculty lab for ~7 weeks

programs.name: Garcia Summer Research Program
programs.eligibility_notes: Lab fee plus housing; states it cannot offer financial aid
programs.notes: Students work toward a research paper/competition entry

programs.name: MITES Summer
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors; US citizens/permanent residents; focus on students from underrepresented and underserved communities
programs.notes: Also MITES Semester (online) for juniors

programs.name: Clark Scholars Program
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors (recent cycles also allowed recent graduates); age 17 by program start
programs.notes: 7-week research in any academic area; no fees, room/board plus stipend; small application fee

programs.name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
programs.eligibility_notes: Sophomores and juniors
programs.notes: Free, includes travel aid; essay-heavy application

programs.name: BU RISE Internship/Practicum
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors
programs.notes: 6-week lab internship; tuition with need-based aid

programs.name: JAX Summer Student Program
programs.eligibility_notes: No longer accepting high school seniors (2026 page); check age minimum
programs.notes: 10-week independent research project; room, board and stipend

programs.name: NIH High School Summer Internship Program (HS-SIP)
programs.eligibility_notes: Age 17+ by start; US citizens/permanent residents; must live within a commuting distance of the campus
programs.notes: Funding and program status has changed in recent years - verify current cycle

programs.name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
programs.eligibility_notes: Age 16+; US citizens/permanent residents; local commuters
programs.notes: 8-week lab placement

programs.name: COSMOS
programs.eligibility_notes: Primarily California students
programs.notes: 4-week cluster courses

programs.name: Ross Mathematics Program
programs.eligibility_notes: Ages ~15-18
programs.notes: Application problems required; number theory focus

programs.name: PROMYS
programs.eligibility_notes: Ages 14+
programs.notes: Free for many families via need-based aid; application problems

programs.name: Canada/USA Mathcamp
programs.eligibility_notes: Ages 13-18
programs.notes: Qualifying Quiz is the main application

programs.name: Hampshire College Summer Studies in Mathematics (HCSSiM)
programs.eligibility_notes: High school students
programs.notes: Application problems

programs.name: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
programs.eligibility_notes: Current 10th-11th graders aged 15-17 on the first day
programs.notes: Admission test plus application

programs.name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
programs.eligibility_notes: Domestic and international students; early and regular rounds
programs.notes: Generous need-based aid

programs.name: MIT Beaver Works Summer Institute (BWSI)
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors; US citizens/permanent residents for most courses
programs.notes: Requires finishing an online prerequisite course before acceptance

programs.name: Bank of America Student Leaders
programs.eligibility_notes: Juniors/seniors in eligible markets; legally able to work in the US
programs.notes: Paid summer internship at a local nonprofit

programs.name: NASA OSTEM Internships (high school)
programs.eligibility_notes: As of Oct 2026 the page requires age 18+ and a high school diploma - effectively graduating seniors; US citizens
programs.notes: Summer, fall and spring sessions each have their own deadline

programs.name: Navy Science & Engineering Apprenticeship Program (SEAP)
programs.eligibility_notes: US citizens; age 16+; within commuting distance of a lab
programs.notes: Window usually opens ~Aug; the 2027-summer cycle closes Nov 30, 2026 (verified Oct 2026). 8 weeks, ~$4,000 stipend, no housing - must live near a participating lab

programs.name: Army Educational Outreach Program (AEOP) apprenticeships
programs.eligibility_notes: Varies by program (SEAP, HSAP, UNITE); many require US citizenship
programs.notes: UNITE is aimed at students underrepresented in STEM

programs.name: AFRL Scholars Program
programs.eligibility_notes: US citizens; age 16+
programs.notes: Paid summer research

programs.name: NIST Summer High School Intern Program (SHIP)
programs.eligibility_notes: US citizens; local commuters
programs.notes: Volunteer (unpaid) research internship

programs.name: Rockefeller University Summer Science Research Program (SSRP)
programs.eligibility_notes: Sophomores not eligible; no housing provided (NYC commuters)
programs.notes: Lab research with mentors

programs.name: Fred Hutch Summer High School Internship Program (SHIP)
programs.eligibility_notes: Rising seniors, 16+, living in the Greater Seattle area; no housing provided; aimed at students from backgrounds underrepresented in biomedical science
programs.notes: 8-week paid lab internship; next cycle info usually posted in November

programs.name: Broad Summer Scholars Program (BSSP)
programs.org: Broad Institute of MIT and Harvard
programs.eligibility_notes: Boston-area high schools (check eligible list)
programs.notes: Paid research in a Broad lab

programs.name: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
programs.eligibility_notes: Age 16+
programs.notes: Paid summer mentorship with a fisheries professional

programs.name: CMU Summer Academy for Math and Science (SAMS)
programs.eligibility_notes: US citizens/permanent residents; focus on students underrepresented in STEM
programs.notes: Tuition-free

programs.name: CMU AI Scholars
programs.eligibility_notes: Juniors at time of applying, 16+ by start; US citizens/permanent residents
programs.notes: Free (tuition, housing, meals); deadline usually early February

programs.name: Princeton Summer Journalism Program
programs.eligibility_notes: Juniors from lower-income backgrounds
programs.notes: Free including travel

programs.name: Iowa Young Writers' Studio
programs.eligibility_notes: Check grade rules per session
programs.notes: Writing sample required

programs.name: Kenyon Review Young Writers Workshop
programs.eligibility_notes: Ages ~16-18 (check)
programs.notes: Writing sample required

programs.name: National Youth Science Camp
programs.eligibility_notes: Juniors/seniors; delegates chosen per state (some states run their own selection)
programs.notes: All-expenses-paid

programs.name: National Security Language Initiative for Youth (NSLI-Y)
programs.eligibility_notes: US citizens; ages ~15-18
programs.notes: Funding status can change - verify the current cycle exists

programs.name: Girls Who Code Summer Programs
programs.eligibility_notes: Girls and non-binary students
programs.notes: Free virtual programs; format changes year to year

programs.name: State Governor's School / state summer institutes
programs.eligibility_notes: Residents of that state; usually school nomination
programs.notes: Many states run free or low-cost programs; search "<your state> governor\u0027s school" and ask your counselor about nomination

programs.name: Federal Pathways Internships
programs.eligibility_notes: Usually 16+ and US citizen; enrolled students
programs.notes: Postings open year-round; filter for high-school-eligible
